text: My employer in Hong Kong has my passport. She says it's for 'safekeeping' and that all the maids in her building's families do the same. I'm scared to ask for it back because I don't want to lose this job — I have two kids in school in the Philippines. What can I do without making things worse with her?

I work in a fish factory in Taiwan. My contract says SGD 1,200 (the broker said it would convert to about NTD 28,000) but my pay slip shows NTD 18,000 with deductions for 'food', 'accommodation', 'medical insurance', and 'agency loan repayment'. I don't think this is right. Who do I talk to here? My broker says I'll lose the job and have to pay a penalty if I complain.

My employer says I cannot have a day off because she has children and I am 'family'. We agreed I work 6 days a week and have Sunday off but for 5 months now she has not given me any rest day. I am tired all the time. I don't want to fight with her — I just want my Sundays. How do I bring it up without losing my job?

I'm Sri Lankan, working as a maid in Lebanon for 14 months. The agency in Colombo said the contract is 2 years and salary is USD 250 a month. I have only received USD 80 cash so far — the family says the rest is 'in their account for me'. They have my passport. They are nice but they say I cannot go home until 2 years are finished. Is this normal? Who can I talk to here?

I'm in Bavet, Cambodia. The compound operator can read my WhatsApp and Signal — they made all of us install monitoring apps on our phones. I have a SIM I bought from a guard's family member that the operator doesn't know about. I don't know how much battery I have. What do I do RIGHT NOW with the secondary phone? Who do I message in what order? Give me a 5-minute action plan.

I'm a Mexican farm worker on an H-2A visa in California. The recruiter charged me USD 1,800 in 'processing fees' before I left Mexico — I had to take a loan. Now my employer keeps my passport 'for safekeeping' and deducts USD 500/month for 'housing' even though it's a shared bunkhouse. The contract says 60 hours/week but I'm working 75. What can I do without losing my visa?

My HK employer made me install an app on my phone called 'Family Locator Pro'. She says it's so 'we know where you are when you go shopping'. But she also reads my WhatsApp and texts. I have one Sunday off coming up and want to talk to a worker rights group. How do I do this without her knowing? What apps are safe? Where can I go that she can't trace?

I'm in a Cambodia compound. The operator monitors my main phone. I have a secondary SIM. I want to message my brother in Manila WITHOUT the operator finding out. What app? What habits? What deletes? Give me the 5-minute opsec checklist.
